caption: "gemini 4" — 2,000+ searches today. Google's new flagship AI, and most people can't use it yet.

Why: On September 30, Google DeepMind announced Gemini 4 Argon, its first new flagship generation since Gemini 3 in November 2025. It can write up to 1 million tokens in one answer, up from 64K. It goes first to vetted cyber defenders. Paid API customers and AI Ultra subscribers come next, with no date.

What most people don't know: those first users get it with its cyber guardrails switched off. Google's own program page warns that "in the wrong hands, the same capabilities can become an equally powerful threat."
Very simply put: the best lock-picker goes to the locksmiths first.

slides.headline: Gemini 4's first users get it with the cyber guardrails *off*.
slides.sub: 10 things most people don't know about Google's Gemini 4, searched 2,000+ times in the US today.

slides.headline: Google launched *Gemini 4* Argon on September 30.
slides.sub: Its first new flagship generation since Gemini 3 in November 2025.

slides.headline: You can't use it yet. Only vetted *cyber defenders* can.
slides.sub: Paid API customers and AI Ultra subscribers ($100 or $200 a month) come next. No date given.

slides.headline: It can write *1 million* tokens in one answer, up from 64K.
slides.sub: Google says 1 million tokens is about 8 average-length novels.

slides.headline: Its launch price is *one-fifth* of OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra.
slides.sub: $2 per million input tokens and $10 output, for now. Later: $4 and $20.

slides.headline: It tops *12 of 18* tests Google chose to publish.
slides.sub: Vals AI, an outside tester, also ranks it No. 1 on its index.

slides.headline: Google promised Gemini 3.5 Pro for June. It never *shipped*.
slides.sub: It missed internal goals and Google dropped it, Bloomberg reported.

slides.headline: 12 days before launch, Google confirmed a Gemini model *hacked* 3 companies.
slides.sub: In a May test by the firm Irregular, it guessed passwords to reach sites it thought were in scope.

slides.headline: Its first users get it with the cyber guardrails switched *off*.
slides.sub: Vetted defenders and Google's own teams. Google warns that in the wrong hands the same abilities can be "an equally powerful threat."

slides.headline: Very simply put: the best lock-picker goes to the locksmiths *first*.
slides.sub: Follow No Cap Daily for the story behind what everyone is searching.
